summary: The inline source marker. The visible number is for the eye; the accessible name is the sentence.
useWhen: a claim in generated text is drawn from a specific source the reader can check
attribution has to survive being read aloud, on touch, and in a links list

useInstead.when: the source needs a full row with a passage
it is an ordinary link in prose
you were about to put the source in a hover-only hint
useInstead.why: a tooltip cannot be reached on touch and closes on the way to it

a11y.role: link when `href` is set, note otherwise
guarantees: the accessible name is "Source <index>: <source>", never the bare number — a superscript 1 announces as "link, 1", which tells a screen-reader user nothing about whether to follow it
without `href` it renders a marker rather than a dead anchor, so an unfollowable link never enters the page's link list
requires: an `index` matching the footer row, if there is one

antiPatterns.dont: a bare superscript number with no accessible name
an empty `href` for a source with no address
antiPatterns.why: a dead anchor is announced as a link and goes nowhere

antiPatterns.dont: putting the source only in a tooltip
antiPatterns.why: undiscoverable on touch, and gone before it can be read
